text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- GAN chairman Jean Jacques Bonnaud refuses to heeed government call to resign over the postponed privatisation of GAN banking subsidiary CIC.
-- Industry chiefs do not believe the economy will pick up in 1997, nor do they expect their investments to rise by more than two percent, INSEE survey shows.
-- Transport Minister agrees to Air France plan to order Boeing aircraft along with European Airbus planes.
-- President Jacques Chirac calls for wider opening of Japanese markets, notably for telecommunications, aircraft and agrifood industries.
-- Pechiney to disengage from food can manufacturing activity.
-- Mandatory CSG tax designed to fill social security deficit to become deductible from income, Budget Minister said yesterday to National Assembly.
-- Axa managing director Gerard de La Martiniere calls for a reform of asset management activity, wants to create a watchdog council for fund managers in France.
-- Financial Markets Council approves share exchange project between Axa and UAP.
-- Tax deductibility for interest of loans designed to buy existing housing could be maintained through end-1997.
-- Lorry drivers strike and demonstrate for improved working conditions.
-- U.S. investment banks are competing to buy real-estate portfolios that burden French banks and insurance companies, seeking to create a European market in asset-backed securities.
